rows.explainer:
GW guesstimate Based on the following administrative data and survey results in DRC and sub-Saharan Africa more broadly, our rough best guess is that roughly 14% of people in DRC would use ITNs in the absence of a mass campaign.

- Demographic and Health Survey (DHS) and Multiple Indicator Survey (MIS) results from other countries in sub-Saharan Africa suggest that the proportion of people who own ITNs from sources other than mass campaigns tends to be ~12%

- The 2018 Multiple Indicator Cluster Survey for DRC suggests that ~40-45% of people used ITNs from sources other than mass campaigns. However, an expert who had looked at the raw dataset from the survey informed us that the data reported in the survey report appeared to be inaccurate and that a coding error was likely to blame. According to this expert, data from the dataset suggested that 78% of ITNs in DRC were from mass campaigns

rows.explainer:
GW guesstimate We apply larger monitoring and evaluation adjustments for distributions in DRC because we believe that DRC is a challenging operating environment in which corruption, insecurity, and poor infrastructure could make ITN loss more likely and/or more likely to go unreported.

While we believe AMF's close coordination with local partners, emphasis on digital data collection, and system to account for and monitor nets during transit mitigates some risk, we are not sure that AMF's systems adequately monitor and validate the last-mile distribution of ITNs to households, and we are concerned that moderate amounts of ITN loss could occur at this stage.
